recognition: Recognized from supplied documentation as UCI Student Performance (UCI 320), the Portuguese-language course records and the cited Cortez and Silva 2008 introduction. Recognition is based on this input; no remembered external result is asserted.
summary: Retain I1 as a revised, proposal-only research idea. The input describes 649 student records from two Portuguese schools, with G1/G2 grades, absences, coarse travel-time categories and support indicators; it lacks dated attendance, support timing, randomized assignment and intervention fidelity. The broker's one computation ran successfully and describes subgroup sizes and G2-G1 summaries under provisional thresholds, which can inform recruitment only. The sole Crossref search returned a limited and mixed-relevance set; it does not resolve whether a close intervention comparison exists. The testable increment remains a prospective equal-scheduled-contact randomized comparison of attendance-access/catch-up support versus subject tutoring, with predeclared baseline-absence moderation.

candidates.title: Separate attendance-access support from tutoring at the first-period decision point
candidates.question: Among Portuguese-course students below a school-predeclared G1 threshold at the end of period 1, does an equal-scheduled-contact attendance-access and missed-lesson recovery offer improve period-2 G2 more than subject tutoring, and is that package contrast larger in a predeclared high-absence stratum?
candidates.new_claim: Support allocation may improve when the added-support package is matched to an attendance-access bottleneck rather than assuming all low G1 reflects subject-mastery difficulty. This is a falsifiable proposal, not a finding in the supplied records.
candidates.input_delta: The input contains G1/G2, total absence count, coarse travel-time categories and support indicators, but no dated lesson attendance, instructional exposure, support assignment, fidelity or randomized comparison. The increment is an equal-contact randomized package contrast with a predeclared baseline-absence interaction.
candidates.domain_value: If the package contrast is meaningfully larger for students with high baseline absence, schools could allocate added support by an actionable risk stratum; if not, a common tutoring route may be preferable. Standard or required support remains available in both arms.
known_basis_refs: official_documentation.additional_info: G1/G2 are first/second-period grades and G3 is final grade; G1/G2 correlate with G3
official_documentation.variables: absences, traveltime, schoolsup, G1, G2
case.workflow: support allocation beyond final-grade prediction
case.unit: two Portuguese schools; support not randomized; limited survey timing metadata
data_profile: 649 rows; absences quartiles 0, 2, 6 and maximum 32; G1/G2 range 0-19
assumptions: The school defines an academically meaningful G1 eligibility threshold and high-absence rule before enrollment; exploratory thresholds are not school policy.
Both added-support offers can have equal scheduled contact minutes, consistent delivery and supplement standard support.
Randomization is feasible within school and risk strata, and classrooms/students support classroom-aware inference.
G2 is scored comparably across arms and aligned with material taught during the intervention.
candidates.variables_and_units: Eligibility: G1 below a predeclared threshold (grade points, 0-20). Moderator: period-1 scheduled Portuguese lessons missed (count), grouped by a predeclared rule. Assigned offer: access-and-catch-up versus subject tutoring (categorical), with equal scheduled contact minutes per student. Proximal outcome: period-2 attended scheduled Portuguese lessons (count and proportion); primary outcome: G2 grade points (0-20). Unit: student; account for classroom/teacher clustering.
candidates.testable_prediction: Frozen before tool returns: the intention-to-treat G2 contrast (access-and-catch-up minus tutoring, estimated with baseline G1 adjustment) will be positive and larger in the predeclared high-absence stratum than in the low-absence stratum. The access package is also predicted to increase period-2 attendance more than tutoring among high-absence students. Attendance improvement without a meaningful G2 advantage does not support the academic-support claim.
candidates.alternative: Subject-mastery difficulty or general contact/attention is the main bottleneck, so tutoring matches or exceeds access-and-catch-up on G2 and the package contrast does not increase with baseline absence. Any attendance difference may fail to translate into learning.
candidates.discriminating_test: Preregister an individually randomized, equal-scheduled-contact comparison among eligible students at period-1 end, stratified by school and predeclared absence group. Keep normal support available in both arms. Record baseline G1 and dated scheduled/attended lessons, assignment, actual package components and minutes, G2, and class/teacher. Estimate intention-to-treat G2 by ANCOVA adjusting for G1, the treatment-by-absence interaction, and attendance contrasts with classroom-aware uncertainty. Set the minimum meaningful G2 difference, missing-data rule and analysis before enrollment. Treat attendance as a proximal outcome; this comparison alone does not identify mediation.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Only exploratory recruitment and descriptive summaries are possible. Existing observational support comparisons cannot estimate causal support effects, attendance response, mediation or prospective outcomes.
candidates.required_new_data: Prospective eligibility and baseline G1; predeclared school threshold and absence rule; dated scheduled and attended Portuguese lessons in both periods; randomized offer and stratum; intervention components, fidelity and delivered minutes; G2; class/teacher identifiers; and a preregistered minimum meaningful difference and analysis plan.
candidates.failure_condition: With adequate precision, reject the routing prediction if the high-absence stratum shows no meaningful G2 advantage for access-and-catch-up over equal-contact tutoring, or if its predicted attendance advantage is absent. If attendance improves but G2 does not, reject the stronger academic-support claim.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Search for secondary-school randomized or quasi-randomized comparisons of attendance/access or missed-instruction recovery support against equal-contact subject tutoring, with baseline-absence moderation, dated attendance and course-grade outcomes.

candidates.title: Test whether a brief student-led needs check improves support matching
candidates.question: At period-1 end, does a structured student conversation identifying a primary barrier and routing to matching existing support improve period-2 support uptake and G2 versus usual referral among students below the school's predeclared threshold?
candidates.new_claim: A brief barrier assessment may improve use of existing support by matching referrals to student-stated needs, even without increasing total support minutes.
candidates.input_delta: The input contains broad support indicators and context variables, but no student-stated need, referral pathway, match quality, uptake timing or randomized routing test.
candidates.domain_value: Schools could improve use of tutoring, attendance or family-contact resources by reducing referrals students do not need or cannot use.
known_basis_refs: official_documentation.variables: schoolsup, famsup, paid, absences, G1, G2
case.workflow: useful support understanding or allocation
case.unit: no randomized support assignment; limited survey timing metadata
assumptions: Students can report a useful primary barrier in a short, non-stigmatizing conversation.
The school has at least two actionable support routes and records offers and uptake.
Usual referral is an ethical comparator and does not withhold standard support.
candidates.variables_and_units: Eligibility by predeclared G1 threshold (0-20); reported barrier (category); offer and uptake (category/yes-no with dates); contact time (minutes); G2 (0-20). Unit: student, clustered by school or class.
candidates.testable_prediction: Compared with usual referral, needs-check students will more often accept and attend the route matched to their reported barrier, with a larger G2 gain if matching improves effective support exposure.
candidates.alternative: The conversation adds attention but does not improve actual match or uptake; any G2 difference reflects contact time or novelty rather than barrier-specific routing.
candidates.discriminating_test: Randomize eligible students to structured needs-check/routing or usual referral, keep available support minutes equal, preregister matched-route uptake as proximal outcome and G2 as academic outcome, and compare intention-to-treat effects. Record non-uptake reasons and whether the route was delivered.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: No causal or matching test is feasible; the input lacks needs, offers, uptake and temporal support routing.
candidates.required_new_data: Student-reported barrier at decision time, referral and offer dates, support type and minutes, uptake and attendance at support, G1/G2, school/class identifiers, and randomized assignment or defensible rollout.
candidates.failure_condition: Reject the matching claim if needs-check does not improve matched-support uptake, or if uptake improvement fails to yield a prespecified meaningful G2 improvement under adequate precision.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Search for randomized school-based student-needs assessment or diagnostic advising that routes adolescents to different support types and reports matched uptake and subsequent course grades.

candidates.title: Compare structured retrieval practice with additional study time
candidates.question: For students with low G1 but adequate attendance, does a short subject-specific retrieval-practice routine improve G2 more than an equal-duration recommendation to add independent study time?
candidates.new_claim: When attendance is adequate, study organization and feedback may matter more than reported weekly study-time category; an equal-time strategy comparison can separate method from time.
candidates.input_delta: The input records ordinal weekly study-time category and period grades, but not study strategy, actual time, practice completion or randomized method assignment. The proposal adds an equal-time contrast and direct exposure measures.
candidates.domain_value: If effective, schools can offer a concrete low-cost study routine rather than broad advice to study longer.
known_basis_refs: case.workflow: understanding or allocating student support beyond generic final-grade prediction
assumptions: Retrieval practice can be delivered for the same time as comparison study.
Students can complete short practice and log duration reliably.
The period-2 assessment covers practiced material.
candidates.variables_and_units: Eligibility: G1 below a predeclared threshold (0-20) and attendance above a predeclared school threshold. Randomized strategy: retrieval practice with feedback versus equal-duration independent study (category). Exposure: completed minutes and practice items (minutes/count). Outcome: G2 (0-20). Unit: student, with class-aware assignment or inference.
candidates.testable_prediction: At equal scheduled study minutes, retrieval practice with feedback will yield a larger mean G2 gain than independent study without requiring a larger study-time dose.
candidates.alternative: Additional structured attention or time, rather than retrieval practice, drives improvement; under equal delivered minutes the G2 difference will be negligible.
candidates.discriminating_test: Randomize eligible students to supervised retrieval practice with feedback or equal-duration independent study, record minutes and completion, use a common period-2 assessment, and compare intention-to-treat G2 with a prespecified minimum meaningful difference.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: No strategy effect is assessable because study method, exposure and randomized assignment are absent. Studytime categories can inform recruitment only.
candidates.required_new_data: Prospective study-strategy assignment, session duration and completion, aligned common G2 assessment, baseline G1 and attendance, and school/class identifiers.
candidates.failure_condition: Reject the strategy-specific claim if retrieval does not exceed equal-time study on G2 by the prespecified meaningful difference, or if delivered exposure is too unequal to interpret the contrast.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Search for secondary-school randomized retrieval-practice interventions versus equal-time independent study, with period-grade outcomes and attendance-conditioned effects.

task.deliverable: L1's focused critique task was completed by R1: sharpen I1, request one descriptive feasibility calculation and one focused prior-work search, then distinguish their evidential scope.
acceptance: Separate randomized package effects from observational description and do not claim identified mediation.
Specify G2 with baseline G1 adjustment, a predeclared absence interaction, equal scheduled contact and an alternative that could defeat the prediction.
Retain standard support; measure dated attendance, fidelity and delivered minutes; account for classroom/teacher clustering.
Use current-data calculation for recruitment feasibility only and interpret Crossref findings only at returned scope.
task.proposed_computation: Executed broker request R1_compute_feasibility: provisional G1<10, absences>=6, cross-tabulated travel categories 1-4; report counts and descriptive G2-G1 t intervals. These cutoffs are data-anchored exploratory probes, not validated eligibility rules.
task.proposed_search: Executed broker request R1_search_access_tutoring: Crossref query for secondary-school randomized or quasi-randomized attendance/access or missed-instruction recovery versus equal-contact tutoring, emphasizing baseline absence, attendance and grades. Returned records did not provide a close verified answer.

critique: R1 correctly noted that package randomization alone does not identify attendance mediation because post-randomization causes may confound attendance and G2.
R1 fixed the primary moderator as predeclared baseline absence; long travel time is context only unless separately powered and preregistered.
Use intention-to-treat G2 with baseline G1 adjustment as primary; raw G2-G1 change is descriptive because of baseline dependence and regression-to-the-mean risk.
Equal scheduled minutes do not ensure equal delivered dose or isolate one mechanism; record package components, fidelity and actual minutes, and interpret the estimand as a package comparison.

final.what_changed: R1 revised the candidate from an attendance-mediation framing to a randomized package-comparison question with attendance as a proximal outcome. It fixed baseline absence as the primary moderator, moved travel time to context, made baseline-adjusted G2 the primary outcome, and required equal scheduled contact plus fidelity/delivered-dose measurement. The feasibility computation informs subgroup recruitment only; the candidate's intervention prediction remains untested.
final.what_is_known: The supplied documentation describes 649 complete student records from two Portuguese schools, with G1/G2 and total absences but no randomized support assignment, dated attendance or reliable intervention timing. The executed descriptive calculation used provisional G1<10 and absences>=6: 157 records met G1<10. For high-absence eligible students, travel-category counts were 28, 17, 3 and 2; for lower-absence eligible students, counts were 43, 43, 18 and 3. The resulting G2-G1 summaries are observational descriptions, not support effects; sparse long-travel cells make travel-time stratification unsuitable as a primary test. Crossref returned eight mixed-relevance records. Two abstracts covered twin-study grade/attendance assumptions and an after-school reading tutoring project; several other hits were title/metadata only, including attendance and supplementary-instruction titles. None verifies the exact proposed package comparison, and the relevance-ordered search is not exhaustive.
final.what_is_new_hypothesis: A predeclared high baseline-absence group may benefit more on period-2 Portuguese grade from attendance-access and missed-lesson recovery support than from equal-scheduled-contact subject tutoring, with a corresponding period-2 attendance advantage. This proposal adds a decision-focused randomized package contrast and moderator beyond the supplied descriptive dataset; no world-literature novelty is established.
final.falsifier: In an adequately powered preregistered trial, the proposal fails if access-and-catch-up does not exceed equal-contact tutoring by the prespecified meaningful G2 amount in the high-absence stratum or if its predicted attendance advantage is absent. If attendance improves but G2 does not, the claim that access recovery is the more useful academic support fails.
final.minimum_next_test: In a prospective cohort of students eligible under a school-predeclared G1 threshold, randomize the access-and-catch-up versus tutoring offer within school and baseline-absence strata while retaining standard support. Record dated scheduled and attended Portuguese lessons, baseline G1, assignment, intervention components/fidelity/actual minutes, G2 and class/teacher identifiers. Preregister the minimum meaningful G2 difference, primary ANCOVA with baseline G1, treatment-by-absence interaction, classroom-aware uncertainty and missing-data handling. First use pilot recruitment counts to ensure each primary stratum can support the precision target; do not select thresholds from outcome contrasts.

R1_search_access_tutoring: returned; relevance-ordered limited Crossref index, no exhaustive novelty verdict
R1_search_access_tutoring_S1-S2: abstracts/metadata on twin-study assumptions and an after-school reading tutoring project; neither directly tests the proposed package comparison
R1_search_access_tutoring_S3-S8: title/date/DOI-only records; no results inferred
final.nearest_work_comparison: The input itself documents prior prediction work using this dataset and its period-grade structure. The returned search includes work concerning attendance, tutoring, and supplementary instruction, but the abstracts and titles available do not establish a close equal-contact attendance-access-versus-subject-tutoring trial with a baseline-absence interaction. This is a limited comparison, not a literature review or verified gap.
final.novelty_status: Input-relative increment: explicit prospective equal-contact package comparison, baseline-absence effect-modification prediction, and G2/attendance decision outcomes are additions to the supplied dataset description and exploratory computation. World-literature novelty: unknown; the single limited Crossref search cannot support a novelty claim.
final.limitations: The computation was descriptive and its uncertainty intervals do not account for sampling design or clustering; it does not estimate treatment effects or validate thresholds. Very small high-absence, long-travel cells are imprecise. The dataset's absence timing is limited, survey/support timing is unclear, and the records are observational. The search was a single relevance-ordered Crossref query with mixed relevance and title-only hits; it is not exhaustive. A randomized package effect would not by itself identify attendance mediation, and package components may differ beyond the intended access mechanism.
